raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it before me. I know this ground — the soil is loamy, the water table is still reachable, and the county extension station has been pushing wheat-corn rotation for as long as I can remember. I'm not going to change what works.

My two sons are in Handan city now. It's just me and my wife. We manage about 12 mu. That's enough for us to handle without hiring too much outside labor, especially now that my back isn't what it was at 40.

**Wheat** goes in come October, after the corn comes off. I'll use a certified improved variety — probably 济麦22, which my neighbor's been using and gets decent yields. I buy new seed every two years; saving my own seed hasn't been worth it since the cooperatives make certified seed cheap enough.

**Summer corn** follows the wheat in June. Hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958. Everyone in the village uses it. Good stalk strength, doesn't lodge badly in the August winds.

Fertilizer: I put down compound fertilizer as a base and then urea as topdress. I probably use more than strictly needed — I'd rather the crop not run short. For wheat I'll do about 18 kg nitrogen per mu across the season. Corn similar. I don't bother testing soil — never have.

Irrigation is the expensive part now. Electricity for the pump keeps going up. For wheat I'll irrigate at sowing, overwintering, jointing, and heading — four times. Corn I'll do twice if it's dry, once if summer rains are decent. I'll watch the sky.

Pesticides: herbicide in early spring for the wheat, fungicide before heading for scab. Corn gets herbicide right after emergence and I'll spray once more if the aphids get bad.

Tillage: rotary after corn harvest, then seed the wheat. I've done no-till once — didn't like it. Too many weeds.
